trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Barcelona Airport at 13:00. Take the Aerobus (€6.75 one-way) or Metro L9 Sud (€5.15) to the city center. Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample. Once settled, take a leisurely orientation walk along Passeig de Gràcia — the grand boulevard lined with Modernista masterpieces. Admire the exteriors of Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) for free from the street to get your first taste of Gaudí's genius.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Eixample neighborhood on foot. Head to the Rambla de Catalunya for an early evening stroll. Grab a seat at a terrace bar for a cold Estrella Damm beer (€2–3). As night falls, wander into the Gaixample area (the LGBTQ+ hub within Eixample) for vibrant street energy and affordable cocktail bars.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at a local bakery near the hotel (€2–4) — or eat on the plane.
meals.lunch: Pick up a bocadillo (baguette sandwich) from a Mercadona supermarket near Passeig de Gràcia for a quick, cheap meal (€2–3).
meals.dinner: Bar Calders (Carrer del Parlament, Eixample) — a beloved local bar with excellent pintxos and tapas from €1.50 each. Budget €10–14 for a full spread with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€12.15) on arrival — it covers all metro and bus trips and will save money throughout the trip. August is hot (30°C+), so carry water and wear sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day early (before the heat peaks) with a visit to the Sagrada Família. Book tickets online in advance (€26 basic entry, or €36 with tower access — worth it for architecture lovers). Spend 2–3 hours exploring Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece, the most iconic building in Barcelona and one of the world's greatest architectural achievements.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic). Wander its narrow medieval streets for free — highlights include the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30 and after 17:15), Plaça Reial, Pont del Bisbe, and the Roman ruins visible through street-level windows. Stop into the Mercat de Santa Caterina (a lesser-known alternative to La Boqueria) to browse colorful produce and grab a cheap snack.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in the Gothic Quarter as it transforms at night. Explore El Born neighborhood just next door — a trendy, artsy district with affordable cocktail bars and great street life. Check out Bar del Convent (free entry, beautiful courtyard) or El Xampanyet for a glass of house cava (€2.50). The streets are buzzing with nightlife energy by 22:00.

meals.breakfast: Granja Viader (Carrer d'en Xuclà, Gothic Quarter) — a historic Barcelona café famous for its orxata and thick hot chocolate with churros (€5–7).
meals.lunch: Mercat de Santa Caterina food stalls — fresh fruit, a slice of tortilla española, and a drink for under €8.
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet (El Born) — classic tapas bar with house cava and anchovy plates. Budget €12–16 including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets at least a few days ahead online to avoid sellouts and long queues. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Gothic Quarter's cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Lesseps or Vallcarca station and hike up to Parc Güell. Entry to the Monumental Zone costs €10 (book online to save time). Gaudí's surreal mosaic terraces and gingerbread gatehouses offer stunning views over Barcelona. Arrive early (opening time ~08:00) to beat the crowds and the heat. The surrounding park areas outside the paid zone are completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back down to Eixample and visit the exterior and ground floor of Casa Milà (La Pedrera) — the rooftop terrace is the highlight but costs €25; instead, admire the extraordinary undulating stone facade for free from outside. Walk to nearby Casa Batlló and Casa Amatller on the 'Block of Discord' (Manzana de la Discòrdia) — all free to view from outside. Pop into the free Fundació Antoni Tàpies (check for free hours) for contemporary Catalan art.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Barcelona's famous nightlife. Eixample has excellent pre-party bars — start at a rooftop terrace bar like La Isabela or a local cocktail bar around Carrer del Consell de Cent. Head to a club in the Port Olímpic area or Poble Sec later (clubs open around midnight; many are free before 01:00 or have free entry with a drink voucher). Sala Apolo and Moog are legendary, affordable venues (€8–15 entry).

meals.breakfast: Federal Café (Carrer del Parlament, Eixample) — popular brunch spot with avocado toast or eggs for €7–10.
meals.lunch: Menú del día (set lunch menu) at a local restaurant near Parc Güell — typically 3 courses with bread and a drink for €10–13. Look for handwritten chalkboard signs.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda (Eixample) — traditional wine bar with cheap tapas and house wine from €2/glass. Budget €10–14.

day_by_day.notes: The menú del día is the best budget hack in Barcelona — a full 3-course meal for €10–13 is standard at most local restaurants Monday–Friday. Take advantage of it for lunch every day.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro or a short bus ride to Barceloneta beach for a morning swim. The beach is free and beautiful. Walk the length of the Barceloneta boardwalk (Passeig Marítim) to enjoy the sea breeze before the afternoon heat. Stop to look at Frank Gehry's golden 'Fish' sculpture near the Hotel Arts — a striking piece of architectural art on the waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Poble Sec and Montjuïc. Take the free escalators up through Poble Sec or the cable car (€11.50 return) to Montjuïc hill. Visit the free Jardins de Laribal and the Fundació Joan Miró (€14, or free on Saturday afternoons after 15:00 — check current schedule). The Castell de Montjuïc offers panoramic views over the city and port (€5 entry). The Pavelló Mies van der Rohe — the legendary 1929 German Pavilion — is a must for architecture lovers (€10).
day_by_day.evening: Poble Sec is one of Barcelona's best neighborhoods for affordable, quality dining and nightlife. Bar Calders, Bodega Sepúlveda, and the many bars along Carrer de Blai (the 'pintxos street') are perfect for a cheap, festive evening. Grab pintxos from multiple bars at €1–2 each. Later, check out a live music venue like Sala Apolo (world music, flamenco, and electronic nights).

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and a pastry from a street vendor or supermarket at Barceloneta (€3–5).
meals.lunch: Menú del día at a local restaurant in Poble Sec — 3 courses with wine for €11–13.
meals.dinner: Carrer de Blai pintxos crawl — visit 3–4 bars and eat pintxos at €1.50–2.50 each. Budget €10–14 including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Montjuïc hosts the Magic Fountain (Font Màgica) light show on Thursday–Sunday evenings (free!) — check the 2027 schedule and time your return from the hill to catch it at dusk. A spectacular free spectacle.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slow final morning in Eixample. Visit the Mercat de l'Abaceria or Mercat de Sant Antoni (a beautifully restored 19th-century iron market) for breakfast among locals — fresh juice, a pastry, and coffee for €4–6. Browse the Sunday book and coin market outside (if it's Sunday). Take a final stroll down Passeig de Gràcia to soak in the Modernista architecture one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, spend remaining time doing any last-minute souvenir shopping at affordable spots — avoid tourist traps on Las Ramblas; instead, try the shops around El Born or Mercat de Sant Antoni for local design and food products. Head to the airport via Aerobus or Metro L9 Sud with plenty of time to spare.

meals.breakfast: Mercat de Sant Antoni — fresh orange juice (€2), croissant or coca de recapte (Catalan flatbread, €2–3), and a café amb llet (coffee with milk, €1.50).
meals.lunch: Final menú del día at a local Eixample restaurant before heading to the airport — a proper Catalan send-off for €11–13.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight — grab a sandwich from a supermarket before departing to avoid overpriced airport food.

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 5 days: Accommodation (pre-booked), Transport ~€25 (T-Casual card + Aerobus x2), Attractions ~€65–80 (Sagrada Família, Parc Güell, Pavelló Mies van der Rohe, Montjuïc), Food ~€70–90, Nightlife ~€30–50. Total estimated spend (excluding flights and hotel): ~€190–245. Barcelona is very walkable — use your feet as much as possible to save on transport.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife at one of the iconic open-air beach clubs near Barceloneta, such as Pacha or Opium Mar. Dance to world-class DJs with the Mediterranean Sea as your backdrop, a quintessential Barcelona night out.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Barcelona Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample by taxi or Aerobus (~35 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll the iconic Passeig de Gràcia from your Eixample base to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — spot Casa Batlló and Casa Amatller facades from the outside. A perfect low-key introduction to Barcelona's architectural gems without booking in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the lively Eixample dining scene for dinner, then explore the Eixample Esquerra (left Eixample) neighborhood known locally as 'Gayxample' for its vibrant bar scene. Enjoy cocktails at a rooftop bar to kick off the trip.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a beloved mid-range tapas bar steps from Passeig de Gràcia. Try the montaditos and patatas bravas (€15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda — a cozy, authentic Catalan wine bar and restaurant in Eixample with excellent value set menus (€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Prioritize rest and acclimatization. August in Barcelona is very hot (30–35°C typically), so stay hydrated and carry water. Book the Sagrada Família guided tour online tonight for Day 2 if not already reserved.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Begin the day at Gaudí's iconic basilica, just a short metro or walk from Eixample. The guided tour reveals intricate architectural symbolism across the Nativity and Passion facades and the breathtaking interior nave. Arrive early (9:00–9:30) to beat the midday crowds and heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Parc de la Ciutadella & Arc de Triomf Walk — Take the metro to Arc de Triomf and walk through the majestic triumphal arch before entering the lush Parc de la Ciutadella. Explore the monumental cascade fountain, the lake, and the peaceful gardens. A great way to decompress after the morning's grandeur.
day_by_day.evening: Wander into the adjacent El Born neighborhood for a tapas crawl and evening exploration of its medieval streets and boutique shops before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Jaume bakery near Eixample — freshly baked pastries, pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato), and coffee (€6–8).
meals.lunch: Bar del Convent inside the El Born Cultural Centre courtyard — affordable Mediterranean plates in a stunning historic setting (€12–18 per person).
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born — a legendary cava bar and tapas spot. Order the house cava and anchovies. Lively and authentic (€20–28 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Sagrada Família tickets well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead, especially in August. Opt for the tower access add-on for panoramic views. Wear comfortable walking shoes; this is a high-step day.

day_by_day.morning: El Born Tapas & Food Market Tour — Join a guided food tour through the El Born neighborhood, exploring the historic Mercat de Santa Caterina (a colorful architectural gem itself), tasting Catalan cheeses, jamón, fresh seafood, and local wines. An immersive morning blending food culture with architectural discovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Barceloneta Beach & Chiringuito Hopping — Head down to Barceloneta after the tour. Spend the hottest part of the day on the beach, then hop between the casual beach bar chiringuitos for cold drinks, fresh seafood, and people-watching along the boardwalk.
day_by_day.evening: Beachfront Club Nightlife Experience — As the sun sets, transition into Barcelona's legendary beach club nightlife. Experience one of the iconic open-air clubs near Barceloneta (such as Pacha Barcelona or Opium) where the party starts around 23:00 and goes until dawn.

meals.breakfast: Included or partially included in the El Born Food Tour (confirm with operator). Otherwise, grab a café amb llet and toast at a local bar (€4–6).
meals.lunch: La Cova Fumada in Barceloneta — a no-frills, cash-only local institution credited with inventing the bombas (potato croquettes). Queue early, it closes by early afternoon (€15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Chiringuito Escribà on Barceloneta beachfront — quality seafood and paella with ocean views before the nightlife begins (€30–40 per person). Pre-book for sunset seating.

day_by_day.notes: The beach club scene starts very late by Northern European standards — dinner at 21:00, pre-drinks at 23:00, clubs from midnight onward is typical. Dress smartly for beach clubs. Keep valuables secure at the beach; Barceloneta can be busy with pickpockets in August.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after the late night — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Mid-morning, visit the Palau de la Música Catalana (a UNESCO World Heritage modernista concert hall by Domènech i Montaner) for a guided architectural tour — a stunning contrast to Gaudí's organic style.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) on a self-guided walk — discover the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, Roman ruins, and hidden medieval alleyways. Browse independent shops and galleries. Consider visiting the MUHBA (Barcelona History Museum) for underground Roman ruins beneath the city.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample for a relaxed evening. Visit a rooftop bar such as La Isabela at Hotel 1898 or the terrace at Mandarin Oriental for sundowner cocktails with skyline views. End with a quiet dinner in the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café — try Alsur Café in Eixample for avocado toast and specialty coffee (€10–14).
meals.lunch: Bar Cañete near the Ramblas — a stylish but accessible tapas bar with excellent Catalan dishes and a lively counter dining experience (€20–30 per person).
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza in Eixample — beloved local spot with creative Neapolitan-style pizzas and natural wines, great for a casual, affordable evening (€18–25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Palau de la Música Catalana tour in advance online. Tours run throughout the morning. This is a great recovery day after the nightlife experience — keep the pace comfortable and flexible.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Funicular de Vallvidrera or the metro up to Park Güell for a morning visit to Gaudí's fantastical hilltop park. Explore the monumental zone (ticketed) with its famous mosaic terrace, dragon staircase, and Hypostyle Room, plus the free forested paths with sweeping views over Barcelona.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Eixample for a final afternoon of leisure shopping along Passeig de Gràcia and Rambla de Catalunya. Browse Spanish fashion brands, design boutiques, and pick up souvenirs. Optionally visit the interior of Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) — both are unmissable Gaudí masterpieces.
day_by_day.evening: Final night celebration — enjoy a farewell dinner at a special restaurant, then head out for one last taste of Barcelona's nightlife in the Eixample bar scene or revisit a favourite El Born spot for cocktails and live music.

meals.breakfast: Granja Viader near the Ramblas — a historic Barcelona institution open since 1870, famous for its homemade cacaolat (chocolate milk) and pastries (€8–12).
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana (revisit) or try Taktika Berri on Carrer de Valencia for outstanding Basque pintxos — a lively lunch counter experience (€15–22 per person).
meals.dinner: Moments or a special splurge dinner at Disfrutar (book months ahead) — alternatively, Honest Greens in Eixample for a fresh, feel-good final meal at a mid-range price (€20–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell's monumental zone requires timed-entry tickets — book online well in advance as August slots sell out fast. Go early (8:00 opening) to enjoy cooler temperatures and fewer crowds. Casa Milà rooftop is especially magical at sunset if you can time an evening visit. Check departure logistics for the following day.

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In: Flight LH lands at 13:00, so the morning is reserved for travel. Take a premium private transfer from Barcelona El Prat Airport to your boutique stay in Eixample. Settle in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity at the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Eixample Architecture Stroll: After settling in, take a leisurely self-guided walk through the Eixample district — the heart of Modernisme. Admire the iconic octagonal city blocks, ornate facades of Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) from the outside. Consider booking a late-afternoon private guided entry to Casa Milà for an intimate architectural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop Aperitivo & Dinner at a Modernista-Inspired Restaurant: Begin the evening with cocktails at a rooftop bar in Eixample offering skyline views. Then dine at Disfrutar or Lasarte — two Michelin-starred restaurants within reach — for a world-class introduction to avant-garde Catalan cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the flight or a light welcome spread at the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Casual but refined lunch at Federal Café or Parking Pizza in Eixample — chic, relaxed, and close to the hotel for a soft landing into the city.
meals.dinner: Tasting menu dinner at Lasarte (3 Michelin stars) or Disfrutar (2 Michelin stars) — pre-book well in advance. Expect €150–€250 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer for a seamless arrival. Reserve dinner weeks in advance as Michelin-starred restaurants in Barcelona fill up quickly, especially in August.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour: Start the day with an exclusive guided tour of Gaudí's masterpiece basilica. Opt for a premium private guide who will decode the intricate symbolism in the facades, stained glass, and forest-like interior columns. Arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat the crowds and experience the morning light flooding through the colored glass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Parc de la Ciutadella & Arc de Triomf Walk: After lunch, head to the lush Parc de la Ciutadella for a refined afternoon stroll. Admire the monumental cascade fountain (partially designed by the young Gaudí), the ornate iron-and-glass greenhouse, and the grand Arc de Triomf boulevard. Rent a rowboat on the park lake for a leisurely, romantic interlude.
day_by_day.evening: El Born Neighborhood Exploration & Cocktail Bar Crawl: Transition into the evening in the trendy El Born district. Explore its medieval streets, then settle into a curated cocktail bar experience — try Bar Paradiso (hidden speakeasy behind a pastrami bar) for world-class mixology.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast or visit Forn de Sant Jaume on Passeig de Gràcia for artisan pastries and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cervecería Catalana on Carrer Mallorca — iconic Catalan tapas with premium ingredients in a stylish setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at El Xampanyet in El Born — a beloved cava bar and tapas institution — followed by a refined meal at Espai Mescladís or Llamber, both celebrated for modern Catalan cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família skip-the-line private tour tickets well in advance — August is peak season and timed-entry slots sell out fast. Wear comfortable shoes for the park walk.

day_by_day.morning: Barceloneta Beach & Chiringuito Hopping: Spend a luxurious late morning at Barceloneta Beach. Arrange a premium sunbed and parasol service through your hotel concierge. Stroll the boardwalk and hop between the best chiringuitos (beach bars) for fresh seafood snacks, cava, and the iconic Barcelona beach atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Sailboat Charter along the Barcelona Coast: Elevate the beach day with a private catamaran or sailboat charter departing from Port Olímpic. Cruise along the coastline with a captain and onboard catering — chilled cava, fresh fruit, and Catalan charcuterie — while taking in the city skyline from the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Beachfront Club Nightlife Experience: As the sun sets, transition directly from the water to Barcelona's legendary open-air beach club scene. Head to Pacha Barcelona or Shôko Beach Club near Barceloneta for a VIP table experience — reserve a bottle service table in advance for premium treatment as world-class DJs take the stage.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before heading to the beach — fresh fruit, yogurt, and espresso.
meals.lunch: Premium seafood lunch at La Mar Salada or Barraca on the Barceloneta seafront — fresh grilled fish, oysters, and local white wine with ocean views.
meals.dinner: Pre-club dinner at Nobu Barcelona in the Hotel Arts — sophisticated Japanese-Peruvian fusion with sleek oceanfront ambiance, perfectly positioned before the nightlife experience.

day_by_day.notes: August nights in Barcelona are warm and vibrant — the beach clubs stay open until dawn. Arrange VIP entry and bottle service in advance through your hotel concierge. Sun protection is essential during the beach morning.

day_by_day.morning: El Born Tapas & Food Market Tour: Join a premium private food tour through the El Born neighborhood and the iconic Mercat de Santa Caterina (a stunning Modernista market with a mosaic roof). Sample artisan cheeses, Iberian ham, fresh anchovies, craft vermouth, and traditional Catalan pastries with an expert local food guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palau de la Música Catalana & Gothic Quarter Architecture Walk: After lunch, visit the UNESCO-listed Palau de la Música Catalana — a breathtaking Modernista concert hall by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Book a private guided tour to appreciate its stained-glass skylight and sculpted facade. Then wander into the adjacent Gothic Quarter to explore its Roman ruins, medieval cathedral, and hidden plazas.
day_by_day.evening: Flamenco Show & Late-Night Jazz: Experience an intimate, high-quality flamenco performance at Palau Dalmases in El Born — a baroque palace setting that elevates the art form. Afterwards, continue the cultural evening at Jamboree Jazz Club on Plaça Reial for live jazz and cocktails in a historic underground venue.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Alsur Café in El Born — specialty coffee, avocado toast, and fresh-squeezed juices in a bright, design-forward space.
meals.lunch: Sit-down lunch at El Xampanyet or Bar del Pla in El Born — traditional Catalan cuisine with excellent natural wines in a lively neighborhood setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bodega Sepúlveda — a refined wine-focused bistro in Eixample with a curated natural wine list and seasonal Catalan small plates, perfect before the evening's cultural events.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Palau de la Música private tour and flamenco show at Palau Dalmases in advance. The Gothic Quarter is best explored in the late afternoon when light filters beautifully through the narrow medieval lanes.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood: Begin the final morning with a private guided visit to Park Güell — Gaudí's mosaic-tiled hilltop park with panoramic views over Barcelona. Arrive early (9:00 AM) with a timed-entry ticket to enjoy the monumental zone before crowds build. Descend into the charming Gràcia neighborhood below for a relaxed stroll through its bohemian plazas and independent boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spa & Wellness at the Hotel or Mandarin Oriental Spa: Dedicate the afternoon to rest and indulgence. Book a signature treatment at the Mandarin Oriental Barcelona's luxury spa — a hammam ritual, deep-tissue massage, or personalized wellness journey — the perfect way to restore after five days of exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Rooftop Nightcap: Conclude the trip with a spectacular farewell dinner at Moments (Mandarin Oriental, 2 Michelin stars) for refined Catalan haute cuisine. End the night with a final cocktail at the rooftop bar of the Hotel Majestic or the Cotton House Hotel — sipping a glass of cava as Barcelona's luminous skyline bids you farewell.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent hotel breakfast — full spread with fresh pastries, cold cuts, eggs to order, freshly squeezed juices, and Catalan cheeses.
meals.lunch: Light, healthy lunch at Parking Pizza or Flax & Kale in Eixample — nourishing and delicious before the afternoon spa session.
meals.dinner: Farewell tasting menu at Moments restaurant inside the Mandarin Oriental Barcelona — a celebration of modern Catalan gastronomy with exceptional wine pairings. Budget €200–€300 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell's monumental zone requires advance timed-entry tickets — book online as soon as possible. Confirm spa appointments 24–48 hours ahead. If departing the following morning, arrange a private airport transfer the night before through the hotel concierge.
